title: Drift results.json
description: One eval run's per-case outcomes. This file is the unit that `drift snapshot` stores immutably against a git commit hash, and the unit `drift diff` compares.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this results schema. Drift accepts any 1.x file. Bump the major version only for a breaking change to the case entry shape.

cases.description: One entry per eval case in the run. `case_id` must be unique across this array; Drift enforces that at validation time (JSON Schema cannot express it).

metadata.description: Free-form run-level metadata. Drift never reads it; adapters may put whatever they like here.

case_id.description: Stable identifier for the eval case. Must be unique within a single results.json, and stable across commits — this is the key `drift diff` matches on. A case_id that changes between runs shows up as a New case plus a silently dropped one.

metric_scores.description: Metric name to numeric score. At least one metric is required. Metric names should be stable across runs; a metric present in one snapshot and absent in the other is skipped when computing that case's score delta.

pass.description: Whether the case passed. Drives the Fixed and Regressed buckets. NOTE for adapter authors: `pass` is a Python keyword, so read it as row["pass"], never row.pass.

environment.description: Where the case was run. `golden_set` is a curated, repeatable eval set; `production_sample` is sampled live traffic.

timestamp.description: When the case was evaluated, ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset (e.g. 2026-09-01T09:46:50Z). Offset is required — naive local times are not comparable across CI machines.

metadata.description: Free-form per-case metadata (prompt text, trace id, latency, ...). Drift never reads it. Put anything non-schema here rather than adding top-level keys — case entries reject unknown properties on purpose, so that extending the contract requires a review.
